sections.h2: Which Screven County offices send and set the tax?
sections.html:
Two desks sit behind every Screven bill. The elected Tax Commissioner mails the bill and takes the money, while the Board of Tax Assessors decides what the parcel is worth. The commissioner's FAQ lists what the office bills: land and buildings, business equipment, motor vehicles, mobile homes and timber.

  • Tax Commissioner, 216 Mims Road #103, Sylvania, GA 30467. Phone 912-564-2206. Hours are weekdays from 8 until 4:45, and title work should be in the door by 4:30.
  • Tax Assessors, 912-564-7918, for returns, value questions and homestead forms.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, at the courthouse, if you need a copy of the deed.

The state revenue department's Screven fact sheet adds that a city may bill its own levy through its clerk. Ask the commissioner whether your parcel carries one.

sections.h2: What is Screven County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Screven is mostly open country. The Census counts 645.78 land square miles and about 22 residents per square mile, and its 2025 estimate of 14,408 people is 2.5 percent above the 2020 base. Sylvania is the town where the tax office operates.

In the QuickFacts comparison, 69.8 percent of households own, the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $124,300, gross rent in the middle is $679, and the typical household earns $52,792. Nearly a quarter of residents, 23.7 percent, are 65 or older, the oldest profile among the four places this batch covers. Only 14.7 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and the average commute runs 30.7 minutes.

Many sellers here are heirs or longtime owners of a modest house. The tax amounts are small next to metro Georgia, yet any unpaid year stays attached to the parcel and grows with interest.

sections.h2: What are the due dates in Screven County, GA?
sections.html:
The commissioner's two pages disagree, so trust the date printed on your bill. The FAQ says real estate and business personal property bills have been due November 15 since 2018. The general information page says December 20.

Late rules posted on the Screven County Tax Commissioner's website
Where postedDueCharges after the date
FAQ pageNovember 151 percent interest monthly, 10 percent penalty after 90 days
General information pageDecember 20Prime plus 3 percent over 12 each month, 5 percent every 120 days up to 20 percent
Mobile homesApril 110 percent penalty

The state fact sheet gives the owner 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest can begin. A USPS postmark counts on mailed payments, and a postage meter stamp does not. Phone the office to confirm your balance.

sections.h2: What does a Screven County lien or levy look like?
sections.html:
Thirty days after the due date, the commissioner may file a fi. fa. with the Clerk of Superior Court. It is a public record, so credit bureaus can see it, and the tax office says it has no say over how they use it.

Next stage: the file goes to a collection contractor and fees of up to $215.00 get added to cover certified notices and a title search. The property is posted and photographed, and a notice runs for four weeks in the Sylvester Local newspaper before any sale, with the printing cost charged to the account.

Pay off the lien before you list, since any title search will turn it up.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Screven County assessment?
sections.html:
Value is fixed as of January 1, and 40 percent of it is taxed. Between January 1 and April 1 you may file a return naming your own figure. Disagreement draws a notice from the assessors, and the clock then runs 45 days.

  • Take the case to the county Board of Equalization, or choose arbitration.
  • Still unhappy, file written notice to continue in Superior Court.
  • Grounds are taxability, value and uniformity. A complaint about the size of the bill is off the table.

Missing a required return costs 10 percent of the value left off. For mobile homes the commissioner's page speaks of a 21 day window for a Board of Equalization appeal after a corrected value. A relative or friend may file for an owner away in the armed forces within 90 days of the value notice.

sections.h2: Which Screven County homestead and relief programs matter?
sections.html:
Own the home and live there on January 1, then file at the assessors' office so the form arrives before April 1. A form that comes in later takes effect the following year. First-time owners bring the warranty deed. After approval the benefit continues without refiling until you move, change the deed or seek a different exemption.

Screven offers local exemptions, and the local figure displaces the state figure when it is bigger. Owners reaching 62 may request one more. The state deferral option covers owners 62 or older with gross household income of $15,000 or under, postponing payment until the property changes hands or the deferred balance reaches 85 percent of market value.

Farm parcels can be assessed at 30 percent, and conservation use land at its use value, each requiring a ten year covenant with the assessors.

sections.h2: How are mobile homes taxed in Screven County?
sections.html:
A mobile home counts as personal property here. If it stands in the county on January 1, the tax is due April 1, and the owner then picks up a location permit and shows a decal. Skipping those steps can mean a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale of the home.

Bills usually mail around January 2. Per the state sheet, a home placed in the county needs its permit within 30 days of permanent placement.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Screven County house that has unpaid tax?
sections.html:
You can. Your closing attorney requests a payoff from the commissioner, and the figure is settled out of your proceeds. A recorded fi. fa. has to be released for the buyer to get clear title.

An all-cash purchase suits inherited, empty or worn houses because no lender inspection stands in the way. Set the offer beside a listing price less repairs and a slower close.

faqs.q: Is the Screven County tax bill due in November or December?
faqs.a: Both dates appear on the commissioner's site: November 15 on the FAQ and December 20 on the general information page. The date on your own bill controls, and 912-564-2206 can confirm it.

faqs.q: Which Screven County office takes homestead applications?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessors' office, reachable at 912-564-7918. The form must arrive by April 1 to count for that year.

faqs.q: What window applies to a Screven County value dispute?
faqs.a: Forty-five days counted from the notice date. The first stop is the assessors, then the Board of Equalization or arbitration.

faqs.q: What is due on a Screven County mobile home each spring?
faqs.a: The annual tax is due April 1, along with the location permit. A 10 percent penalty follows a missed date.

faqs.q: Can Screven County seniors postpone tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Homeowners 62 or older with gross household income of $15,000 or less may defer, and the deferred amount stays owed until ownership changes or it reaches 85 percent of market value.
